An object moves with speed $v_1$, $v_2$, and $v_3$ along a line segment AB, BC and CD respectively as shown in figure. Where AB = BC and AD = 3AB, then average speed of the object will be :
solution: AB = BC = CD = $x$. $\langle v\rangle = \dfrac{3x}{\frac{x}{v_1} + \frac{x}{v_2} + \frac{x}{v_3}} = \dfrac{3v_1v_2v_3}{v_2v_3 + v_1v_3 + v_1v_2}$

stem: A 12.5 eV electron beam is used to bombard gaseous hydrogen at room temperature. The number of spectral lines emitted will be:
solution: The electron can transfer up to 12.09 eV, exciting hydrogen to $n = 3$. Number of spectral lines $= \dfrac{3(3-1)}{2} = 3$

stem: At any instant the velocity of a particle of mass 500 g is $(2t\hat i + 3t^2\hat j)\ \text{ms}^{-1}$. If the force acting on the particle at $t = 1$ s is $(\hat i + x\hat j)$ N. Then the value of x will be:
solution: $\vec a = 2\hat i + 6t\hat j$; at $t = 1$, $\vec a = 2\hat i + 6\hat j$. $\vec F = 0.5(2\hat i + 6\hat j) = \hat i + 3\hat j$. Hence $x = 3$

stem: In a reflecting telescope, a secondary mirror is used to:
options: reduce the problem of mechanical support
move the eyepiece outside the telescopic tube
solution: The secondary mirror reflects light out of the tube to the eyepiece. It has the advantage of a large focal length in a short telescope.
